newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICAN COACH ENDORSES LIONS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICAN COACH ENDORSES LIONS.

text.p: Leading South African rugby coach Harry Viljoen has given the British Lions a ringing endorsement on the eve of his team's meeting with the tourists in Cape Town on Saturday.

The Western Province coach said he believed the Lions played better rugby than any Super 12 side in their opening tour match against Eastern Province last week. Viljoen's Province take on the Lions at Newlands on Saturday.
"I may be the only guy in South Africa who thinks this but if the Lions put it together they will be awesome," said Viljoen of the opening 39-11 win.
"The way they are playing the game, the continuity, the running into space, running lines, popping the ball in the tackle, recycling it -- I haven't seen that in Super 12 games.
"People talk about a lack of aggression in their forwards but I'm sure it will be there. Once they mould into a unit they are going to give the Springboks a really tough time."
He dismissed Wednesday's mudbath in which the Lions struggled to overcome lowly Border, 18-14.
"For one the conditions were against them and secondly that was their Wednesday team and there's a big difference between them and the team we will be playing," he said.
"What I really like about them though is that they have got a formidable coaching team who know what they're doing -- a real brains trust with Ian McGeechan, Jim Telfer and Andy Keast."
In his fledgling coaching career, Viljoen has taken both Transvaal (now the Gauteng Lions) and Natal to the Currie Cup final.
Now in his first season with Western Province he has steered them to the low-key Nite Series title with 11 straight victories against admittedly weak opposition.
"This will be our first real test and already I have seen the players 20 to 30 percent more keyed up and enthusiastic in training," said Viljoen.

His side includes six Springboks but it lacks an established half-back pairing although Percival Montgomery -- pressed into duty at fly-half but normally a centre -- has been one of the stars of the South African season to date.
Lions tour manager Fran Cotton said: "This is going to be our most formidable opposition to date.
"Western Province are in good form and have some good players. We are not underestimating them at all."
The Lions have named a side containing 10 Englishmen and although Cotton stressed it was not the test side the majority of the team probably already have their names inked in.

Skipper and lock Martin Johnson makes his first appearance of the tour as do number eight Tim Rodber and hooker Barry Williams with only Irish prop Paul Wallace of the 35-man squad yet to start a match.

Western Province - 15-Justin Swart; 14-James Small, 13-Robbie Fleck, 12-Dick Muir (captain), 11-Simon Berridge; 10-Percival Montgomery, 9-Stephen Hatley; 8-Andrew Aitken, 7-Robby Brink, 6-Corne Krige, 5-Hottie Louw, 4-Fritz van Heerden, 3-Keith Andrew, 2-Andrew Paterson, 1-Garry Pagel.

British Lions - 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-John Bentley, 13-Jeremy Guscott, 12-Allan Tait, 11-Ieuan Evans; 10-Gregor Townsend, 9-Rob Howley; 8-Tim Rodber, 7-Richard Hill, 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Martin Johnson (captain), 3-Jason Leonard, 2-Barr Williams, 1-Graham Rowntree.
